articles.title: Workspace overview
articles.description: Learn how projects, people, and workspace settings fit together.

blocks.text: A workspace holds the projects and people who work together. Each project has its own members, status, and updates. Workspace settings apply to all projects unless a project has a specific override.
Start with one workspace for one team. Give it a name that people recognize. You can add more projects as the work grows without creating another workspace.

items: Projects organize a defined piece of work.
Members can belong to several projects.
Workspace owners manage access and shared settings.

blocks.text: Choose a role based on the work a person needs to do. A Viewer can read shared work. An Editor can update project content. An Admin can also manage workspace settings.
A project can limit which workspace members see its content. A workspace role alone does not add someone to every private project.

items: Check your workspace name and profile.
Create a project for the current piece of work.
Invite the people who will contribute.
Set your notification preferences.

blocks.text: The overview shows recent project activity. Use it to find changes since your previous visit. Project pages contain the full history and the current work.

articles.title: Create your first project
articles.description: Set up a project with a clear purpose and an owner.

blocks.text: A project should describe one outcome that the team can recognize as complete. Pick an owner who can answer questions about scope and progress.

items: A short, specific name.
A description of the intended outcome.
An owner who belongs to the workspace.

blocks.text: Project names are visible to project members. Do not place private customer information in a project name.

items: Open Projects and select Create project.
Enter the name and choose an owner.
Check the summary and select Create.

blocks.text: New projects start as Active. The project appears at the top of the list. Add a description before you invite other people so they understand what the project is for.
Open the new project and confirm that its owner and name are correct. Add the first work item and invite the people who need to contribute.
Keep the initial scope small. You can add work items later without changing the project purpose.

articles.title: Manage notifications
articles.description: Choose the events and summaries that you want to receive.

blocks.text: Comments, mentions, project updates, and invitations can each create a notification. Enable only the categories that help you keep track of your work.

items: Comments and mentions concern a specific discussion.
Project updates describe status or milestone changes.
Invitations tell you about new workspace or project access.

blocks.text: An email summary combines recent activity in one message. Daily summaries cover the previous day. Weekly summaries group the previous week. Turning summaries off does not change your event notification choices.
Changing summary frequency does not send an email immediately. The new choice applies at the next scheduled delivery.

items: Change the event categories or summary setting.
Review the Unsaved changes message.
Select Save changes and wait for confirmation.

blocks.text: Reset restores your most recently saved settings. It does not necessarily restore the original defaults.

articles.title: Use project statuses
articles.description: Keep the project list useful with a small set of clear states.

blocks.text: Status describes the project as a whole. It does not need to change whenever a single work item is blocked. Add an update when the reason for a status change would help the team.

items: Open the project you want to update.
Choose the new status.
Add a short update explaining the change.

blocks.text: Pause a project when work has stopped but the team expects to return. Complete it when the intended outcome is delivered. You can reopen a completed project if its scope needs another change.
Completing a project keeps its content and history. It does not delete the project.
Review paused projects regularly. A short note about the next decision helps the team know whether to wait, resume, or close the work.

items: Name the decision or dependency that stops progress.
Assign a person to follow up.
Record the date of the next review.

articles.title: Command reference
articles.description: Find the commands used in local workspace examples.

blocks.text: The project list command returns the projects available in the selected workspace. Use a status filter to reduce the result. These examples are documentation only; the reader does not execute commands.

workspace projects list --status active
workspace projects list --status paused

rows: Limit results to a project status

blocks.text: Use a project ID to inspect one project. IDs remain stable when a project is renamed. Copy the ID from the project details before using a command.

workspace projects show prj_help_center
workspace projects members prj_help_center
A project name and a project ID are different values. The show command expects the ID.
Structured output is useful for local scripts. Check the status and ID fields before using a record in another operation.

items: id is the stable project identifier.
name is the visible project name.
status is the current project state.

blocks.text: First check which workspace is selected. Projects belong to a workspace and can be hidden by search text or a status filter. Clear the filters before asking someone to change your access.

items: Confirm the workspace name.
Clear search text and status filters.
Ask the project owner to check membership.

blocks.text: A missing project does not necessarily mean that it was deleted.
Wait for the save confirmation before leaving a page. A field error can prevent saving even when other values are valid. Correct the field with the error and submit again.
Do not repeatedly submit while the interface shows a saving state. The current request must finish before another save begins.
Include the workspace name, project ID, expected result, and actual result. A short sequence of steps is more useful than a general description that something failed.

Workspace: Northstar
Project: prj_help_center
Action: Change status to Active
Expected: The status changes
Actual: A save error appears

items: Do not include passwords or private tokens.
Include the exact error text.
State whether the problem repeats.
